references.text: The Lord speaks to Moses in similar words and asks why he is crying out to Him instead of taking action. Both texts show that prayer alone is insufficient when God requires action.
The Lord informs Moses about the people's sin, just as He here informs Joshua that Israel has sinned. Both situations involve God revealing the people's transgression.
The Lord commands Moses to rise and go down from the mountain because the people have acted corruptly. The same command to stand up is given to Joshua here.
The warning about devoted things that would bring a curse upon Israel's camp. Joshua 7:10 is the direct consequence of this warning being ignored.
Describes Joshua falling on his face before the ark of the covenant, which is the action the Lord refers to when He says 'get up'.
